title: MCP Governance & 2026 Evolution
content:
## Overview

The Model Context Protocol (MCP), originally released by Anthropic in November 2024, has undergone significant governance changes and technical evolution. In December 2025, Anthropic donated MCP to the Linux Foundation, making it a vendor-neutral open standard. The protocol's 2026 specification introduces stateless architecture, formal Tasks support, and an Extensions framework.

---

## Governance: The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)

On December 9, 2025, Anthropic donated MCP to the **Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)**, a directed fund under the Linux Foundation. The foundation was co-founded by Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI — direct competitors aligning on shared infrastructure.

**Founding platinum members:** Amazon, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI

**Founding projects:**
- **MCP** — contributed by Anthropic
- **goose** — contributed by Block
- **AGENTS.md** — contributed by OpenAI

The donation means the MCP specification is now governed by a multi-vendor foundation rather than a single company. Changes to the protocol require community consensus, and any AI framework can implement MCP without depending on Anthropic's roadmap decisions.

This mirrors the governance model of standards like HTTP, USB-C, and TCP/IP — competing companies co-maintaining infrastructure they all need.

---

## Server Ecosystem Growth

| Period | Approximate public server count |
|---|---|
| November 2024 (launch) | ~10 official reference servers |
| Mid-2025 | Hundreds |
| Early 2026 | **500+** |

The community adds new MCP servers weekly. Major coverage areas as of 2026:

- **Databases:** Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB
- **File storage:** Google Drive, Box, Dropbox, S3
- **Dev tools:** GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Asana
- **Communication:** Slack, email, Discord
- **Web:** Puppeteer, Playwright, Brave Search, general web scraping
- **Cloud infrastructure:** Docker, Kubernetes, AWS and GCP CLI tools
- **Finance:** SEC EDGAR access, financial data feeds

The canonical server list is maintained at [github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers).

---

## 2026 Specification Updates

The 2026 MCP specification (release candidate: July 28, 2026) introduces several major changes:

### Stateless Protocol Core

The most significant architectural change: **MCP is now stateless at the protocol layer.** Previous MCP connections maintained server-side session state, which made horizontal scaling of MCP servers difficult — each request had to hit the same server instance that held the session. The 2026 spec moves session state to the client, allowing MCP servers to scale like ordinary stateless HTTP services behind a load balancer.

### Tasks

A first-class primitive for long-running, asynchronous operations. The original MCP protocol was designed around request/response cycles that complete in seconds. Tasks expose operations that take minutes or hours — with built-in status polling, progress reporting, and cancellation. This is essential for agentic workflows that invoke slow external processes (e.g., running a CI pipeline, training a model, processing a large document batch).

### Extensions Framework

A formal mechanism for adding capabilities to MCP without breaking backward compatibility. Extensions let niche or experimental features be adopted incrementally — a server can advertise an extension; clients that understand it can use it; clients that don't can ignore it.

### MCP Apps

A packaging format that bundles an MCP server, its configuration, and its required permissions into a deployable unit. This addresses a practical friction point: setting up an MCP server currently requires manually cloning a repo, configuring credentials, and updating the host client's config file. MCP Apps aim to make server installation closer to a one-click operation.

### Authorization Hardening

Updated OAuth authentication flows to improve security in multi-server environments where a single agent connects to many MCP servers simultaneously.

---

## Cross-Vendor Adoption

A key outcome of AAIF governance is adoption beyond Claude. As of 2026, MCP is supported by:

- **Claude Code** (official Anthropic CLI)
- **Claude Desktop**
- **VS Code and JetBrains** (via extensions)
- Multiple third-party agent frameworks
- Enterprise deployments on AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure

This cross-vendor adoption is the goal the AAIF governance structure was designed to accelerate: vendors are more willing to invest in MCP server development when the protocol is controlled by a neutral foundation rather than a competitor.
